personality_one_liner: A calm, precise, instrument-like workbench that prioritizes modular data density and mono-spaced visuals over decorative flair.

spacing.rule: Handle spacing correctly dont have extra spaces where its not required, handle padding and margin corectly and subtle for buttons and components

dont's: Do not use blur/glass, use solid surfaceSecondary or borders for elevation

screens.name: Today Home
screens.purpose: A modular dashboard answering 'what matters?' first with attention summaries and visual-heavy tiles (rings, gauges).

states.empty: Empty workbench illustration with 'Add Module' CTA
states.error: Inline module error state with retry icon

screens.layout: Left-aligned header. Global search bar at top. Grid of modular summary tiles below. Visuals (SVG rings/gauges) take precedence over text. Use thick structural dividers and mono-spaced metrics.

screens.name: Attention Center
screens.purpose: Groups Urgent, Upcoming, and Info items, offering a 'Why?' explanation sheet and resolution actions.

states.empty: Clean 'All caught up' workbench graphic in center

screens.layout: Strict list layout categorized by Urgent/Upcoming/Info. Each row has clear actions (done/snooze/dismiss). Tapping an item opens a bottom sheet with 'Why?' explanation. Status icons always accompany text.

screens.name: Vehicles Module
screens.purpose: Dashboard for vehicle mileage, service countdowns, and fuel logs with trend charts.
screens.layout: Top section: Vehicle selector. Main: Dashboard with prominent SVG mileage gauge and service countdown bars. Bottom: Fuel log history. Left-aligned mono-spaced numbers.

screens.name: Money Module
screens.purpose: Budget ring, category breakdowns, and transactions with a quick-entry numpad.
screens.layout: Large SVG budget ring at the top. Category breakdown bars beneath. Sticky 'Quick Entry' FAB opens a bottom sheet with a custom numpad and category chips.

screens.name: Quick Tools
screens.purpose: Fast utility calculators (unit converter, date calc, EMI) acting as a workbench.
screens.layout: Segmented controls or a side-scrolling list of tool chips. Content area updates immediately based on tool selection. High data density, dense numpads.

screens.name: Settings & Module Library
screens.purpose: Manage app theme, accent colors, density modes, and enable/reorder modules.
screens.layout: Standard categorized settings list. Module library uses drag-and-drop handles for reordering. Theme and accent pickers are inline horizontal scrolling lists.

mosaic_bg.alt: Abstract geometric wave mosaic for Tessera theme

instructions_to_main_agent: Strictly follow the user's explicit choices: 'Tessera' product name, Comfortable/Dense density modes, and status NEVER shown by color alone (always pair with icons).
This app is a local-first utility. Emphasize a 'workbench' feel: calm, precise, instrument-like. Avoid 'SaaS dashboard' clutter.
Visuals (SVG rings, gauges, trend lines, countdown bars) must be placed BEFORE text in the hierarchy.
Use 'JetBrains Mono' for all data, metrics, and gauges, and 'Inter' for UI labels. Download the TTF files from Google Fonts GitHub directly into the assets folder.
Use @react-native-vector-icons/MaterialIcons as requested. Do NOT use emojis.
Charts must be implemented natively using react-native-svg.
Implement the UI with a left-aligned layout and clear hierarchy. Use Bottom Sheets (@gorhom/bottom-sheet) extensively for quick entries.
Shadows should be removed (tier 0). Rely on subtle borders (1pt max) and background tonal shifts to separate modules and lists.
Allow user to select accent color; the default defined here is an earthy Ochre (#D68E42). Do not use blue or purple for any accents.
Research takeaway: Soft card stacks with rigid internal data structure provide the best balance between calm usability and data density. Prioritize modular content.
